content: ZoroDos
Discard one, draw two
Concept

Zoroark GX is widely known to be the boogeyman of early Sun & Moon formats, not for its overwhelming power but for its brutal efficiency, creating wins on card and board advantage. This version of the deck was played by Philip Schulz to Harrogate Regionals, including a 4-2 Gyarados line to counter popular Blacephalon GX and heavy counts of disruptive cards like Enhanced Hammer, Pal Pad and Acerola for the mirror.
The Deck
Decklist on LimitlessTCG
List credit to Philip Schulz at Harrogate Regionals 2018.
Core Pokemon
4-4 Zorua, Zoroark GX

This deck intends to get atleast 3 Zorua down turn 1, gaining access to the powerful “Trade” on turn 2. Zoroark GX is the main attacker and draw engine in this deck, and so having as many as possible on board at all times keeps you playing the game.

Zoroark GX's 210HP is surprisingly tanky, allowing you to engange most decks in 2HKO wars with “Rioutous Beating”. “Trade” allows you to aggressively dig through the Deck, setting up healing plays to outlast and win said war. “Trade” requires you to make many decisions throughout the game, however in this deck you can shortcut those decisions if you do not yet have 3 Magikarp in the discard, as those are premier discard targets.
(3-1)-2 Magikarp, Gyarados

3 of the Magikarp have the “Submerge” Ability, which prevents them from taking damage on the Bench, useful against Buzzwole GX and Alolan Ninetales GX. The final Karp has no Ability, such that you might play it down against Weavile decks and have 1 fewer Ability in play.

Gyarados' “Venting Anger” deals 50x the number of Magikarp in your Discard pile. With 150HP as a single-prize attacker this Gyarados can hit reliably for 150 Damage, OHKOing Water weak Blacephalon GX and stretching with Choice Band to KO Tapu Lele GX. Furthermore, once all the Magikarp have been discarded with “Trade”, Ditto {*} can be evolved into a final Gyarados that deals a massive 200 Damage, as all Magikarp are in the Discard pile.
In matchups where Gyarados is not particularly needed, bench just 1 Magikarp and Ditto {*}, such that you might have access to 2 Gyarados if need arises.
This full combo deals 250 Damage to Pokemon GX
2 Tapu Lele GX

Tapu Lele GX is an Ultra Ball and Mysterious Treasure searchable out to any Supporter card in the deck with its “Wonder Tag” Ability. Turn 1 this can grab an Elm's Lecture, a Judge in the midgame, or it can fetch the game winning Guzma on the last turn. You can also attack with “Energy Drive” out of desperation. Although there are 2 in the list, Tapu Lele is a liability on the Bench so take care to not bench it where unnecessary, and have a plan to Acerola it out of play if it ever gets pinged.
Tech Pokemon
1 Ditto {*}

Ditto {*} acts as an extra copy of your evolving Basic Pokemon, and it can be evolved into whichever the situation calls for. Play it down to have a more flexible board which can react to an opponent's play. Ditto {*} is the only way in this list to get Alolan Muk into play.
Alolan Muk

“Power of Alchemy” shuts off Marshadow, Xurkitree GX, Hoopa, Oranguru, Giratina, Diancie {*}, Ditto {*}, Marshadow GX, Passimian and Dawn Wings Necrozma GX to name a few. Powerful particularly against those wall strategies it denies, Alolan Muk allows you to shut off Pokemon that might help your opponent, whilst not denying yourself much. Its hefty 4 Retreat can be Guzma'd around, so this bench-sitter is a real thorn in your opponent's side. Note that evolving into Alolan Muk does shut off the bench barrier effect on your Magikarp.
1 Marshadow

No one likes a turn 1 “Let Loose”. With the draw power of Zoroark GX, you can always replenish a hand after using “Let Loose”. Save Marshadow for combo turns where you would rather not play Judge as your Supporter for turn.
Oranguru

The deck only plays 4 Energy, but doesn't always expect to win in 3 attacks. Oranguru's “Resource Management” recycles Energy, disruptive Supporters and switching outs at a ridiculous rate, allowing you to have enough to close out against control matchups, or just loop enough Enhanced Hammer to fly through the mirror.
Trainers
Elm Engine and Setup

The not only needs Pokemon on Bench for “Rioutous Beating”, but also it needs a wide board of Zorua, with Magikarp in the Discard. To ensure as many Pokemon Turn 1 the deck plays a full 4 copies of Professor Elm's Lecture, which can be searched by Tapu Lele GX if not in the opening hand. Further copies of Elm can be used to fish the Magikarp out of the deck. 2 Cynthia give you enough cards to find Evolutions and combo pieces, whilst comfortably discarding some to draw.
4 Ultra Ball, 4 Timer Ball and 1 Mysterious Treasure are the Item Pokemon search cards in the deck, giving you more than enough outs to find Zoroark GX and Gyarados pieces.
Each Timer Ball is 2 Zoroark trust me
Other Trainers
3 Guzma is a high enough count that you can consistently find them to swing into the targets you actually want to hit.

3 Acerola is a strong card that allows you to reset a damaged Pokemon, usually Zoroark GX, back to hand. Rebench the retrieved Zorua and attach to your next Zoroark GX to get ahead whilst maintaining your Energy and board.

2 Judge allows you to hand disrupt when necessary, try to use it on turns where your opponent really needs to hit a combo to make a play next turn, or aggressively turn 2 against an opponent with a slow start.
2 Kukui and 3 Choice Band allow you to get extra damage in against Pokemon GX, hitting +50 Damage can net KOs on important 200HP targets with Gyarados.
1 Tate & Liza gives you a Tapu Lele searchable way to move a trapped Pokemon without gusting or required it be damaged, whilst also offering a shuffle draw in a pinch.
3 Enhanced Hammer is loopable for the mirror with Oranguru, but often is best used to just remove an Energy and gain tempo.
2 Pal Pad allow you to loop Acerola, Judge & Guzma to have access to them almost every turn.
1 Rescue Stretcher allows Oranguru to go infinite against decks without Lugia GX or Girafarig, though most often its used to recover Pokemon discarded by “Trade”.

1 Max Potion allows you to remove damage from a Pokemon, without taking up your Supporter for turn. The downside of losing your Energy is easily shrugged off by attaching a DCE from hand and announcing “Rioutous Beating”.
Energy

4 Double Colorless Energy aren't searchable in the deck, so having a max count makes drawing them off Trade more consistent. All of your attackers can be powered up with 1 DCE, as long as you manage attachments well you will have enough to win a game.
